source_definition: Relates a security control, activity or security practice to the managed/protected object it protects.
target_definition: Links a requirement element or security mechanism to the security property or safety objective it protects.
classification_reason: Both express protection, but their permitted subjects and protected objects differ.

source_definition: Associates a programme or organisation with a role that exists within its SbD governance or delivery context.
target_definition: Links a person or organisation to a source-defined SORA actor role it bears.
classification_reason: Both assign roles, but the SbD relationship includes programmes as well as organisations.

source_definition: Relates an activity or organisational concept to a record, inventory or documented evidence item it creates or maintains.
target_definition: Links an actor or system to a Record or Log that it records or maintains.
classification_reason: Both concern record creation or maintenance, but the target is restricted to records and logs.

source_definition: Relates a monitoring activity to risk, controls, remediation, capabilities, mechanisms or other monitored subjects.
target_definition: Links an actual actor or system to a system, service, performance characteristic, condition, log, or threat context that it monitors.
classification_reason: Both express monitoring, but their domains and monitored subjects differ.

source_definition: A component acquired for a programme or capability and considered in cyber-resilient design.
target_definition: A hardware, software, material, equipment, or other constituent element relevant to the UAS or support system.
classification_reason: Same component concept, but scoped to different operational domains.

source_definition: A normative standard used to guide design, development or assurance.
target_definition: A standard used as an accepted design, process, training, or assurance reference.
classification_reason: Equivalent normative standard concepts.

source_definition: Human error as a socio-technical contributor to cyber risk.
target_definition: A human action/error capable of adversely affecting the safety of the operation.
classification_reason: Same human-error concept, with cybersecurity and operational-safety scope differences.

source_definition: The Defence acquisition/development/delivery programme within which SbD activity is governed across the capability lifecycle.
target_definition: A structured organisational programme maintained for a defined assurance purpose.
classification_reason: Both represent programmes, but their acquisition and assurance scopes differ.

source_definition: A service acquired, used, supported or exited as part of programme delivery.
target_definition: A service that supports UAS operations or assurance activities.
classification_reason: Same service concept in different programme and operational contexts.

source_definition: An organisational entity that owns, governs, staffs or performs programme or security activities.
target_definition: An organisational actor participating in the SORA assurance or UAS operational context.
classification_reason: Equivalent organisational-actor concepts.

source_definition: A technical or socio-technical system subject to acquisition, use, exit, risk assessment or security controls.
target_definition: A technical system considered by SORA requirements.
classification_reason: SbD includes socio-technical systems, while SORA focuses on technical systems.

source_definition: An action, process or practice performed to satisfy or support SbD requirements.
target_definition: A performed action, process, or event relevant to satisfying or evidencing a SORA requirement.
classification_reason: Equivalent performed activity or process concepts.

source_definition: A document, record, plan, assessment, inventory, reference or other information-bearing artefact used in programme delivery or assurance.
target_definition: A data, document, record, or assurance artefact that can be created, maintained, reviewed, or supplied as part of SORA assurance.
classification_reason: Equivalent information-bearing artefact concepts.

source_definition: A cybersecurity property or objective that SbD requirements seek to protect or achieve.
target_definition: A protected cybersecurity attribute or capability, such as confidentiality, integrity, availability, authenticity, or resilience.
classification_reason: Equivalent protected cybersecurity-property concepts.

source_definition: Risk arising from cybersecurity threats, vulnerabilities, dependencies or failures that may affect programme capabilities or essential functions.
target_definition: Risk arising from cyber threats affecting the UAS operation or its supporting systems.
classification_reason: Equivalent cybersecurity-risk concepts.

source_definition: Information essential to programme functioning or security that may be stored, transferred, inventoried, protected or compromised.
target_definition: Data or information relevant to the UAS, operation, or assurance activities.
classification_reason: Same data concept, but with different domain scope.

source_definition: A lifecycle stage or cross-lifecycle context in which an SbD requirement may apply.
target_definition: A controlled lifecycle or operational context in which a requirement, activity, or assurance expectation applies.
classification_reason: Equivalent lifecycle or operational applicability contexts.

source_definition: A cybersecurity principle or recognised practice expressed by the SbD requirements.
target_definition: A named cybersecurity principle or practice referenced by the Cyber Safety Extension.
classification_reason: Equivalent cybersecurity principle or recognised-practice concepts.

source_definition: A technical or procedural mechanism used to provide a security or resilience function.
target_definition: A security mechanism or control approach such as access control, encryption, anti-replay, digital signatures, hashes, malware protection, or wireless protection.
classification_reason: Equivalent technical or procedural security-mechanism concepts.

source_definition: A potential for adverse consequence considered in programme cybersecurity decision-making.
target_definition: A SORA-relevant risk combining likelihood/frequency and consequence/severity.
classification_reason: Equivalent general risk concepts.

source_definition: Indicates an activity that must be performed to satisfy an SbD requirement.
target_definition: States that satisfaction of a SORA requirement entails an activity or process of the specified type.
classification_reason: Both require an activity, but SORA points to a controlled activity type.

source_definition: Associates an SbD requirement with the official SbD criterion/evidence area from which it originates.
target_definition: Links a SORA requirement element to its source criterion.
classification_reason: Equivalent links between requirement elements and their source criteria.

source_definition: Relates an SbD requirement to a managed/protected object or organisational context to which the obligation applies.
target_definition: Associates a SORA requirement element with the source-defined actor role responsible for or directly subject to the requirement.
classification_reason: A general applicability relationship is broader than responsibility assigned to an actor role.

source_definition: Associates an organisational concept with an activity it performs.
target_definition: Links an actual actor to an actual performed assurance, operational, maintenance, training, audit, or other activity.
classification_reason: Both express activity performance, but organisational concepts and actual actors have different scope.

source_definition: General obligation relationship indicating that an SbD requirement calls for an activity, security practice, control or other domain element.
target_definition: Links a SORA Assurance requirement to evidence that must be available, documented, provided, or produced.
classification_reason: The general SbD requirement relationship is much broader than requiring evidence.

source_definition: Indicates a security principle or recognised practice required or expressed as an obligation by an SbD requirement.
target_definition: Links a requirement element to a named SORA/Cyber Extension security principle or practice it explicitly requires or incorporates.
classification_reason: Equivalent requirement-to-security-principle relationships.

source_definition: Indicates that a concept, artefact or decision is derived from another source statement, assessment or artefact.
target_definition: Links an official or analytical requirement element to the controlled SORA source document from which it was derived.
classification_reason: Both express derivation, but SORA is restricted to controlled source documents.

source_definition: Indicates a security control that is required by an SbD requirement.
target_definition: Links a requirement element to a security mechanism or control that the source requires or explicitly identifies.
classification_reason: Security controls and security mechanisms perform the same requirement-supporting role here.

source_definition: Associates an SbD requirement directly with its official SbD principle.
target_definition: Links a SORA requirement element to the Operational Safety Objective it supports.
classification_reason: Both express structural membership, but an SbD principle and a SORA OSO are different groupings.

source_definition: Links an SbD requirement to a threat, vulnerability, risk, adverse event or related risk concept addressed by it.
target_definition: Links a requirement element or activity to a risk, threat, hazard, failure, human error, event, or adverse condition that it addresses.
classification_reason: Equivalent links from requirements or activities to addressed risk and threat concepts.

source_definition: Data whose location, movement and compromise effects require explicit understanding.
target_definition: Data whose compromise or unavailability can affect safety-critical activities.
classification_reason: Safety-critical data is a specialised form of critical data.

source_definition: Staff or personnel performing programme, security, operational, disposal, response or recovery activities.
target_definition: A human actor participating in the SORA assurance or UAS operational context.
classification_reason: Personnel and person overlap, but personnel represents a workforce grouping.

source_definition: Relates an activity, decision or assurance artefact to an information resource, artefact, asset, control or method it uses.
target_definition: Links a requirement, activity, or assurance artefact to a Standard or Means of Compliance used to substantiate satisfaction.
classification_reason: The SbD uses relationship is broader than using a standard or means of compliance.

source_definition: A concept describing cyber threats, adversarial scenarios or assumptions.
target_definition: A risk, hazard, failure, threat, event, or condition relevant to SORA safety or cyber safety.
classification_reason: Threat Concept is a narrower part of the broader RiskAndThreatConcept grouping.

source_definition: An adversarial role whose objectives, perspective or actions are considered in threat analysis.
target_definition: A source-defined role that an Actor may hold, such as Applicant, Operator, Remote Pilot, Supplier, or Competent Authority.
classification_reason: A threat actor is adversarial, while ActorRole includes many non-adversarial roles.

source_definition: The operational circumstances in which capabilities are provided and used.
target_definition: A non-actor element describing an operational boundary, configuration, resource, or environmental condition.
classification_reason: Both describe operational context, but SORA excludes actors from this class.

source_definition: A cyber threat or threat condition that informs risk appetite, assessment and security decisions.
target_definition: A controlled type of cybersecurity threat or attack referenced by the SORA Cyber Safety Extension.
classification_reason: ThreatType is a controlled category of the broader Threat concept.

source_definition: Links an atomic requirement clause candidate back to its official parent SbD requirement.
target_definition: Links a higher-robustness requirement element to lower-robustness requirement content explicitly inherited through 'Same as Low/Medium' constructs.
classification_reason: Parent-clause membership is not equivalent to inheritance between robustness requirements.

source_definition: The programme security plan requested as an assurance artefact.
target_definition: A documented plan for a defined operational, organisational, or response purpose.
classification_reason: Security Plan is a specialised type of Plan.

source_definition: A design standard into which lessons learned and improvement information may be incorporated.
target_definition: An Airworthiness Design Standard used for UAS components essential to safe operations.
classification_reason: Airworthiness Design Standard is a domain-specific type of Design Standard.

source_definition: Evidence that required personnel training has been delivered, maintained or assessed.
target_definition: A retained record of training completed or competence evidence.
classification_reason: Both represent retained evidence of completed training or demonstrated competence.

source_definition: Indicates that a capability or activity contributes to a Defence strategic objective or essential function.
target_definition: Represents conformity of a UAS, configuration, manufacturing output, process, or evidence item to design data, a standard, specification, or other source-defined reference.
classification_reason: Contribution to an objective is not equivalent to conformity with a standard or specification.
